title: Helmsman: Failure Probe Inspector — compact trace snapshots & retry composer
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Design a compact, single-pane inspector that surfaces an actionable snapshot of a failed request and lets operators compose safe retry attempts. The Helmsman view should balance maximum signal density with minimal cognitive load: quick failure cause hints, reproducible payload snippets, quick toggles for retrying with/without KV cache, and an automated confidence score for suggested fallback routings.
background: Current request detail UX forces users to open multiple panels (payload, trace timeline, retry controls) to triage simple transient errors. Support teams repeatedly ask for a condensed workflow for quick retries and hypothesis testing that preserves telemetry and prevents accidental data resends. We want a single entry point for rapid triage and controlled retry composition that fits into the existing console routing and rollouts flows.
goals: Create a compact inspector that summarizes failed requests in one pane
Provide safe, reversible retry composition with clear telemetry impact
Expose quick hypothesis toggles (skip cache, reduce batch size, swap model variant)
Integrate with rollouts so retries respect canary and fallback policies
user_stories: As an oncall engineer, I want to see a concise failure summary and the top three likely causes so I can decide whether to escalate or retry
As an SRE, I want to compose a retry that excludes prefix cache and limit tokens without leaving the inspector so I can test a mitigation quickly
As a PM, I want suggested fallback variants surfaced with confidence so non-expert operators avoid unsafe model swaps
acceptance_criteria: Helmsman view loads within 300ms for a sampled failed request (matching Console perf SLO)
Failure summary includes error class, top-3 correlated signals, and a one-line remediation hint
Retry composer has toggles: preserve_kv_cache (on/off), honor_rollout (on/off), token_limit (slider), model_variant (dropdown)
Retry action triggers a sandboxed call path visible in the request timeline and does not alter the original stored payload
Design handoff includes annotated Figma frames and a clickthrough prototype covering retry approval flow
notes: We scoped down to a single-pane approach after discovery: users prefer fewer context switches during oncall
Telemetry contract: retry actions must emit 'retry.composed' event with metadata: toggles used, operator id, and sandbox id
Backend will expose a read-only sandbox token allowing dry-run retries visible only to allowed roles
design_feedback: PM review (Priya Desai): prefer explicit 'dry-run' vs 'execute' distinction—make buttons different colors and add hover tips
Eng review (Marcus Huang): ensure retry composer UI maps 1:1 to the existing retry API parameters; avoid free-text fields
SRE feedback (Lena Ortiz): add a 'replay with tracing' toggle so we can sample traces without triggering downstream side-effects
decisions: Decision: Use a two-state retry flow (Dry-run -> Promote) rather than immediate execution to reduce accidental resends
Decision: Surface 'confidence score' computed by backend ML as a three-tier label (Low / Medium / High) instead of raw probability
Decision: Keep payload viewer collapsed by default; show a 3-line snippet with 'Expand' to full payload to reduce noise
next_steps: Finalize annotated Figma screens and add micro-interaction specs (button states, error-tooltips)
Work with ENG to add 'retry.composed' telemetry event in next API iteration (ENG-3187)
Schedule cross-functional review (Design + Eng + SRE) on 2026-03-17 to sign off on safety flows
